men-only-hotels.title: Men Only Hotel Blackpool: 3 Stays | Blackpool.gay
men-only-hotels.description: Looking for a men only hotel Blackpool trip? Compare three men-only stays by the Rainbow Quarter, with house rules, walking times and tips on who each suits.
men-only-hotels.h1: Men-only hotels and guest houses in Blackpool
men-only-hotels.intro: Three Blackpool stays are men-only, all within a few minutes of the gay bars; here is how they differ and who each one suits.
men-only-hotels.body_html:
If you are searching for a men only hotel Blackpool has a small, well-established choice. All of the options below sit on or just off Lord Street, so you step outside and you are in the Rainbow Quarter. Each one has its own house rules, so read the notes before you commit.

Which Blackpool hotels are men-only?

Three stays in our listings are men-only and adults-only:

  • The Prince Albert Hotel on Yates Street: a discreet hotel that keeps a low profile on the street, with themed weekends. Our research lists seven en-suite rooms across three floors, reached by stairs only. Walk to Blackpool North station: about 5 minutes.
  • Trades Hotel and Bar on Lord Street: a members' hotel and late bar in joined townhouses, with the bar open daily 11am to 3am on the listed hours. Walk to the station: about 3 minutes; to Mardi Gras: about 1 minute.
  • Welhorny's on Banks Street: a private members' naturist guest house with a bar, themed weekends and bear-friendly nights. Walk to the station: about 3 minutes; to Funny Girls: about 2 minutes.

How do they compare?

StayFeelBest for
The Prince Albert HotelQuiet, discreet, smallA calm base with a lounge bar and breakfast
Trades Hotel and BarBig, sociable, late-running barStaying right where the nights end
Welhorny'sMembers' rules, naturistGuests who know the naturist and bear scene

What does men-only actually mean here?

It means men only and 18 or over, and at Trades and Welhorny's you are asked to follow members' arrangements for your stay. Do not turn up expecting to bring a guest of another gender, and read the policy when you book. Our research notes that Trades has seen a recent licence transfer and change of supervisor, so ask the hotel directly about current management and facilities. At the Prince Albert, reception hours were described inconsistently in listings, so confirm check-in arrangements before you travel.

Is a men-only hotel right for me?

Choose one if you want a stay with no mixed-group noise, a bar downstairs that suits your crowd, and the scene on your doorstep. If you would rather share the trip with friends of every gender, look at our adults-only guest houses instead; most of them welcome everyone over 18.

Planning around your stay

  • Add a late night: Man Bar and Growlr Club runs a men-only cruise club on the upper floor; entry is by wristband, collected at the downstairs counter.
  • Show night: Funny Girls is a two to five minute stroll from all three stays.
  • Access: all three have stairs, and none lists a lift, so mention mobility needs when you book.

When should I book?

Book early for Pride and the Illuminations; see our Pride weekend hotel guide and the 48-hour weekend plan. For full venue background, the Rainbow Quarter reference site goes deeper.

Practical notes before you book

Men-only stays tend to suit travellers who know exactly what they want from a weekend, so it helps to ask a few questions up front. Ask whether breakfast is included, what time you can check in, and what the bar arrangements are for residents. The Prince Albert lists check-in from 3pm and check-out by 10:30am in our research, and it lists a no-smoking, no-pets policy with free wifi.

Think about your own comfort too. Welhorny's is a naturist guest house, which is a very different proposition from a quiet hotel with a breakfast room. Trades is large, with around 60 rooms in our research, so you get a sociable crowd rather than a boutique feel.

Pair your stay with a sauna visit

Two men's saunas sit within a few minutes of these hotels: Acqua Sauna on Springfield Road, two minutes from the station, and W3 Complex on Charles Street. Both are men only and 18+, and opening times vary, so check their own sites before you go.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

adults-only-guest-houses.title: Adults Only Gay Guest Houses Blackpool | Blackpool.gay
adults-only-guest-houses.description: Find an adults only hotel in Blackpool that welcomes LGBTQ+ guests: guest houses and bars with rooms, grouped by style, with walking times to the bars.
adults-only-guest-houses.h1: Adults-only gay guest houses in Blackpool
adults-only-guest-houses.intro: Looking for an adults only hotel Blackpool gay visitors recommend? These guest houses and bars with rooms are all 18+, with walking times from each.
adults-only-guest-houses.body_html:
An adults-only stay means no children's noise at breakfast and a quieter landing after a big night. Blackpool's gay guest houses cluster around Lord Street, Cocker Street and Dickson Road, so most are a short stroll from the bars. Here is the full list, grouped by style.

Which are the adults-only guest houses?

LGBTQ+ guest houses

  • Westfield House: small, quiet, Edwardian, four-star rated, with discounted parking vouchers and non-smoking rooms. About 6 minutes to the station.
  • Lawrence House: four-star, aimed at LGBTQ+ guests and their pals, with a roof terrace and dinner on the listing. Check-in 2pm to 10pm; about 4 minutes to The Flying Handbag.
  • Chaps Hotel: an established LGBTQ+ hotel on Cocker Street: themed bedrooms, breakfast, and a bar downstairs. About 5 minutes to the station.
  • Q Accommodation: boutique, room-only, seven suites, booked through Mardi Gras. About 2 minutes to the station.

Adults-only B&Bs with a bar

  • The Dragonfly: a B&B-style stay with a bar of its own, on Lord Street. It changed hands recently, so confirm what is included.
  • The Belvedere: a Victorian-era guest house along Dickson Road, with a following among LGBTQ+ guests. A sale has been reported, so confirm it is trading.
  • Evanescent Bar and Rooms: a laid-back bar with budget rooms on Cocker Street.
  • McGraths Bar and Hotel: 18+ rooms above a lively drag bar, with guests praising hosts, cleanliness and breakfast.

Modern and bar-led

  • Hotel Neon: a modern hotel next to a cocktail bar with a garden, on Yates Street.
  • Peek-a-Booze: budget rooms above a cabaret bar on Dickson Road.

Are all gay guest houses in Blackpool adults-only?

No. Pride Lodge on High Street and De-Lovely Hotel on Lord Street are LGBTQ+ guest houses where we have not recorded an adults-only rule, so ask when booking if that matters. Mardi Gras and Rendezvous also have rooms without a recorded age policy in our data.

Which one is quietest?

Westfield House and Lawrence House are the calmer picks: the first is tagged as quiet, the second is set back from the main drag. Anywhere above a bar, such as McGraths or Peek-a-Booze, is the opposite: ideal if you want to fall into bed after the last song.

Booking notes

  • Stairs: several listings state upper floors by stairs only, with no lift.
  • Parking: Lawrence House has no on-site parking, and nearby car parks are the answer.
  • Groups: Westfield House is listed as declining stag and hen parties; see our group planning guide.

Prefer men-only? See men-only hotels. Or browse every option on the main stays page.

Choosing between guest houses and bars with rooms

A guest house gives you a landlady-or-landlord welcome, a breakfast table and usually an earlier night. A bar with rooms gives you a late-night downstairs and the sound of the party until closing. Neither is better; it depends on whether you want the weekend to start at the bar or finish at it.

If breakfast matters, De-Lovely's breakfast is highly rated, Chaps lists breakfast, and McGraths guests praise theirs. If you want a drink on the premises without leaving the building, Chaps, The Dragonfly and The Belvedere all list a bar.

Planning your first evening

Most of these stays are a few minutes from Mardi Gras and Funny Girls. Use the walking times above to decide how far you want to go, and read our first weekend plan for how to pace it.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

gay-owned-guest-houses.title: Gay Guest House Blackpool: LGBTQ+ B&Bs | Blackpool.gay
gay-owned-guest-houses.description: Which Blackpool B&Bs describe themselves as LGBTQ+? An honest look at what our records say, what they do not, and how to ask before you book a stay.
gay-owned-guest-houses.h1: Gay-owned and LGBTQ+-run B&Bs in Blackpool
gay-owned-guest-houses.intro: Our records describe several guest houses as LGBTQ+ stays; here is what is confirmed, what is not, and how to ask before you book.
gay-owned-guest-houses.body_html:
Plenty of visitors want their money to stay in the community, so "gay-owned" is a fair thing to search for. We want to be straight with you: our data records which stays are LGBTQ+ guest houses, but it does not record who owns them. So we will not label any property gay-owned. What we can do is list the guest houses that describe themselves as LGBTQ+ and show you how to ask.

Which guest houses describe themselves as LGBTQ+?

  • Pride Lodge: on High Street facing the station, listed with a private sauna, a gym, and a seasonal hot tub. Reception is staffed 10am to 7pm Monday to Saturday and 11am to 5pm Sunday, with WhatsApp out of hours.
  • De-Lovely Hotel: a Lord Street stay with quirky, themed bedrooms, a breakfast that reviewers like and a cocktail bar anyone can use.
  • Westfield House: LGBTQ+, adults-only, four-star rated, on Lord Street.
  • Lawrence House: welcoming LGBTQ+ guests plus their mates, with dinners and a roof terrace in the listing.
  • Chaps Hotel: an LGBTQ+ hotel on Cocker Street with a bar and themed rooms.

Are these places gay-owned?

We cannot say. Being an LGBTQ+ guest house tells you about the welcome and the clientele, not the ownership structure. Some properties also belong to the BAGS Blackpool hoteliers group, which vets its members as LGBTQ+-friendly stays; membership is a friendliness marker, again not an ownership one.

How can I check who runs a place?

  1. Check the property's own site or social pages; many hosts introduce themselves.
  2. Ask at booking: most guest houses are happy to explain who you will meet at reception.
  3. Read recent guest reviews, which often mention the hosts by name.

McGraths is a good example: visitors score it well on welcome, tidiness and the morning meal, which tells you about the welcome even if it does not tell you about ownership. See McGraths Bar and Hotel.

What if I want a bar and rooms in one place?

Take a look at stays above the bar, where the rooms sit over a community pub or cabaret bar.

Making a good choice

  • Want quiet: Westfield House or Lawrence House.
  • Want sauna facilities on site: Pride Lodge, as listed.
  • Want breakfast and cocktails under one roof: De-Lovely.

For all adult-only choices read adults-only gay guest houses. The Rainbow Quarter reference site also covers community businesses in more depth.

What to look for instead of an ownership label

If you want a stay that feels part of the community, look for evidence you can check. Does the guest house describe itself as LGBTQ+ on its own site? Does it list a clear policy on age and groups? Does it point you towards local bars, shows and Pride? Those signals tell you more than a label.

Pride Lodge advises booking early for Pride and Illuminations weekends. Lawrence House presents itself as a home for LGBTQ+ guests with companions. De-Lovely runs a bar open to the public, which makes it a social stop as well as a place to sleep.

A note about accuracy

Our facts come from the owner's records and published listings. If you know a property's ownership and would like it described correctly, tell us via the forum and we will check it.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

hotels-with-a-bar.title: Blackpool Gay Bars With Rooms | Blackpool.gay
hotels-with-a-bar.description: Want to sleep where the party is? Gay bars with rooms in Blackpool, including Peek-a-Booze, Mardi Gras, Trades, Neon and Lu-Lu's, with walking times.
hotels-with-a-bar.h1: Stay above the bar: gay pubs with rooms in Blackpool
hotels-with-a-bar.intro: Sleep upstairs from the music at one of several Rainbow Quarter bars with rooms; here is what each offers and how to choose.
hotels-with-a-bar.body_html:
The simplest way to do a Blackpool gay weekend is to book a room in the bar. No taxis, no late walk, and the stairs are the last obstacle of the night. Several Rainbow Quarter venues run rooms, and each has a different mood.

Which bars have rooms?

  • Peek-a-Booze at 72-74 Dickson Road: keenly priced 18+ rooms upstairs from a cabaret bar. Food daily 9am to 7pm on listed hours. About 3 minutes to Funny Girls.
  • Mardi Gras at 41-43 Lord Street: a pub with three separate rooms with cabaret, karaoke and Sunday roasts. About 3 minutes to the station.
  • Trades Hotel and Bar (51-55 Lord Street): men-only, with a bar listed open daily 11am to 3am. Men only and 18+.
  • Hotel Neon (15 Yates Street): an adults-only hotel with a cocktail bar and a garden, usually open Thursday to Sunday.
  • Lu-Lu's Cabaret Lounge at 78b-82 Dickson Road, with roughly 26 en-suite rooms and two bars side by side. Bring cash. About 4 minutes to Funny Girls.
  • Rendezvous Bar and Rooms (15-17 Lord Street): a compact bar with bedrooms near the station, closing at around 10pm on listed times.
  • McGraths Bar and Hotel, Evanescent Bar and Rooms and The Dame Lane: further bars with rooms, with drag, karaoke or bingo.

How noisy are rooms above a bar?

Expect music on show nights. Peek-a-Booze lists bingo and karaoke across the week, Lu-Lu's has cabaret Friday to Sunday from 7pm, and Mardi Gras is listed until 3am at the weekend. If you want sleep, ask for a room away from the bar or choose Rendezvous, which closes early. If you want to be part of it, pick Peek-a-Booze, or Mardi Gras.

Can I bundle a room with a show?

Peek-a-Booze suggests asking about room-and-show deals if you are staying for Funny Girls just up the road; Funny Girls is about 3 minutes away on foot. Ask any property what packages exist before you pay.

What about stairs and accessibility?

Most of these properties have upper floors reached by stairs only; both Peek-a-Booze and Mardi Gras say there is no lift, while Lu-Lu's has steps up at the door. Phone ahead if you have mobility needs.

Which should I choose?

  • Lively and cheap: Peek-a-Booze or Lu-Lu's.
  • Community pub with food: Mardi Gras.
  • Quiet cocktails and rooms: Hotel Neon.
  • Men-only: Trades.

Prefer a guest house with no bar? See adults-only gay guest houses, or check the hotels near Queen Street.

Questions to ask before you book a room over a bar

  • Which floor is the room on, and is there a lift? Several properties have none.
  • What time does the bar close on your stay nights? Mardi Gras is listed to 3am on Fridays, weekends vary.
  • Does the bar take cards? Lu-Lu's is listed as cash only.
  • Can I check in when the reception is not staffed? Ask about the process for late arrivals.

Eating where you sleep

Mardi Gras along with Peek-a-Booze both list food, and the Sunday roast at Mardi Gras suits a lazy last day; book ahead on busy weekends. Peek-a-Booze lists food daily from 9am to 7pm.

Making the most of it

Bars with rooms are a relaxed way to do the Rainbow Quarter. You can nip upstairs to change between the show at Funny Girls and the late bars, and you are never far from your bed. If you want the full picture of nightly entertainment, see what's on.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

near-queen-street.title: Hotels Near Queen Street Blackpool | Blackpool.gay
near-queen-street.description: Hotels near Queen Street Blackpool, ranked by walking minutes to The Flying Handbag: gay guest houses, bars with rooms and adults-only stays in one table.
near-queen-street.h1: Gay-friendly hotels a short walk from Queen Street
near-queen-street.intro: Queen Street is the late-night strip; these stays are the closest, with walking times to The Flying Handbag, the strip’s flagship bar.
near-queen-street.body_html:
Queen Street is where Blackpool's late nights land. If you want to roll home in minutes, pick a stay close to The Flying Handbag at number 44. The times below are walking minutes from each stay to that bar.

Which stays are closest to Queen Street?

StayWalk to The Flying HandbagType
Pride Lodge1 minuteLGBTQ+ guest house
Rendezvous Bar and Rooms1 minuteBar with rooms
Q Accommodation2 minutesAdults-only suites
Mardi Gras2 minutesPub with rooms
Welhorny's3 minutesMen-only
The Blackpool North3 minutesPublic bar with rooms
Lawrence House4 minutesAdults-only guest house
Trades Hotel and Bar4 minutesMen-only
Peek-a-Booze4 minutesRooms above a cabaret bar
Evanescent Bar and Rooms4 minutesBar with rooms

What is on Queen Street itself?

The Flying Handbag is the purpose-built flagship, with a sun terrace, food and karaoke, and its listed events include Monday Mayhem from 8pm until 3am, QuizMania on Wednesdays, Thirsty Thursday and a Friday night with Miss Amber. Check current times before you go; see our nightlife guide for other bars.

Is there a good stay for quiet sleepers near the strip?

Lawrence House is on a quiet street, four minutes from the strip, with dinners on offer and a roof terrace. Q Accommodation is two minutes away and room-only, so you will want breakfast elsewhere.

Do I need to stay close?

Not necessarily. Everything in the quarter is compact: even The Dame Lane, the furthest listed stay, is 8 minutes from The Flying Handbag. Choose by mood and budget first, and distance second.

Tips

  • Funny Girls is 1 to 3 minutes from the nearest stays for an early show, then walk to Queen Street.
  • Look at stays near Blackpool North station if you arrive by train.
  • Cabs can be found at the station and outside Funny Girls.

More reference detail on Queen Street is available on Rainbow Quarter reference site.

How the walk feels

The times in the table are walking minutes between the stay and the bar. They are short because the quarter is compact: from most stays on Lord Street you can reach Queen Street in less time than it takes to order a taxi. Walk in a group when you can, keep to well-lit streets and read our safety page.

Before the strip

Mardi Gras is two minutes from The Flying Handbag and Garlands is a little further on Talbot Road, so a classic crawl is Lord Street first, then Queen Street. The bars on Dickson Road, including Funny Girls (about 2 to 6 minutes from these stays), fit in earlier in the evening.

After the strip

Because the listed stays are all within 8 minutes of The Flying Handbag, you can keep the night going at Queen Street's pace and still be in bed shortly after. Stay in a bar with rooms if you want even shorter: see hotels with a bar.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

near-blackpool-north-station.title: Hotels Near Blackpool North Station | Blackpool.gay
near-blackpool-north-station.description: Arriving by train? Gay friendly hotels near Blackpool North station, ranked by walking minutes, with notes on parking, reception hours and nearby bars.
near-blackpool-north-station.h1: Gay-friendly stays near Blackpool North station
near-blackpool-north-station.intro: Arriving by train? These LGBTQ+ stays are the shortest walks from Blackpool North, with minutes from the platform exit to each door.
near-blackpool-north-station.body_html:
Blackpool North is the main railway stop, right at the edge of the quarter. If you are travelling light, you can be at your guest house within minutes. Here are the stays, with walking times worked out from the owner's coordinates.

Which stays are nearest to the station?

StayWalk from station
Pride Lodge1 minute
Rendezvous Bar and Rooms2 minutes
Q Accommodation2 minutes
Mardi Gras3 minutes
Trades Hotel and Bar3 minutes
Welhorny's3 minutes
The Blackpool North3 minutes
Evanescent Bar and Rooms4 minutes
Chaps Hotel5 minutes
The Prince Albert Hotel5 minutes
Lawrence House5 minutes
Peek-a-Booze5 minutes

Which is the best arrival stay?

For a first-time visitor, Pride Lodge is hard to beat on distance: one minute from the station, with listed reception hours of 10am to 7pm Monday to Saturday and 11am to 5pm Sunday. If you arrive later, they list WhatsApp out of hours. The Blackpool North is a handy first stop with a public bar open from midday.

What can I drop into right away?

  • Garlands on Talbot Road: free entry, and resident queens from mid-afternoon on the listed times.
  • Funny Girls: about two minutes from the station.
  • The Flying Handbag: noon opening on the listed hours.

What if I am arriving by car instead?

You do not need a station-side stay. Pride Lodge sells parking passes at reception that you must buy before parking; Westfield House offers discounted parking vouchers; Lawrence House has no on-site parking. Read our getting there and getting home guide for all options.

Are the walks step-free?

We have no step-by-step accessibility data for the routes, and several of the stays have stairs. Check the individual stay page, and see our Queen Street stays for the next ring out.

Travelling light or with luggage

If you have a case, the stays within three minutes are your friends: Pride Lodge, Rendezvous, Q Accommodation, Mardi Gras, Trades, Welhorny's and The Blackpool North. The rest are still only a few minutes further. Check-in times differ, and Lawrence House lists check-in from 2pm to 10pm; ask about left-luggage if you arrive early.

Trains and trams

Trains and trams both arrive at Blackpool North, and the tram stop is by the station. We do not list timetables, so use National Rail and Blackpool Transport for times, and read getting there and getting home.

Leaving

Allow extra time on departure day, particularly after a big night, and book a taxi in advance if you have an early train. Taxis wait at the station.

Which station stay is best for what?

  • Solo traveller wanting company: The Blackpool North, a public bar open from midday until late, or Mardi Gras.
  • Couple wanting a smart base: Q Accommodation, with seven suites, booked through Mardi Gras.
  • Quick late-night route home: Rendezvous or Pride Lodge.

Remember that stays differ on lifts and steps. Q Accommodation has two steps to the entrance and no lift, and Pride Lodge and Trades list no lift information in our data, so phone ahead.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

budget-stays.title: Cheap Gay Hotels Blackpool | Blackpool.gay
budget-stays.description: Budget gay friendly hotels Blackpool visitors can book: simple B&Bs and rooms above bars, the one published price, and practical ways to keep costs down.
budget-stays.h1: Budget stays for a gay weekend in Blackpool
budget-stays.intro: You can stay in the Rainbow Quarter without a big bill: these simpler stays and bar rooms suit tighter budgets, with the one listed price.
budget-stays.body_html:
Blackpool is already one of the better-value places for an LGBTQ+ weekend, and the quarter has a handful of simpler stays. We only quote one price because it is the only one published in our data: rooms at Lawrence House from about £50 with breakfast. For everything else, treat the descriptions as guides and check rates directly.

Which stays are described as budget or simple?

  • The B&B Blackpool: a no-frills B&B with its own little bar, also on Cocker Street. Pre-book the £5 parking if driving; the two attic singles have limited headroom.
  • Peek-a-Booze: budget adults-only rooms above a cabaret bar on Dickson Road.
  • Lu-Lu's Cabaret Lounge: cabaret bar with around 26 en-suite rooms at a modest price. Take cash for the bar.
  • Evanescent Bar and Rooms: budget adults-only rooms above a laid-back bar.
  • Trades Hotel and Bar: a large men-only hotel with free breakfast listed in our research; reviews are mixed, with the bar praised and some guests reporting room condition issues.
  • Lawrence House: about £50 with breakfast, four-star, adults-only.

How do I keep the cost down?

  1. Go midweek or in spring and winter, the cheapest periods in our season notes. See quiet midweek breaks.
  2. Pick a stay close to the bars so you skip taxis; most are 1 to 6 minutes from the station.
  3. Choose a free night: Garlands has free entry and daily drag.
  4. Ask Peek-a-Booze about room-and-show deals if you are seeing Funny Girls.

What is cheap to do while you are here?

Free bingo runs on Wednesday evenings at Peek-a-Booze, with Play Your Cards Right at 9pm, and Garlands lists no entry charge, daily, with queens on stage from the afternoon. Funny Girls standing tickets start around £10, and seats run from roughly £17 up to £35 by night; see planning a drag night.

Are budget stays safe and welcoming?

They are LGBTQ+ venues, so the welcome is a given, but simple means simple. Several have stairs only, and some rooms have limited headroom or a steep staircase. Read each stay's page, and our safety page for late-night tips.

When is the best time to book?

Pride weekend and Illuminations weekends fill first and rooms cost most; check Pride weekend hotels. Everything else is a better bet for bargains.

What simple means in practice

A budget stay trades facilities for price. Expect stairs rather than lifts, smaller rooms and fewer extras. The B&B Blackpool and Evanescent are simple stays with a bar attached, while Peek-a-Booze and also Lu-Lu's keep the entertainment downstairs.

Parking and extras

If you are driving, The B&B Blackpool lists a £5 parking option you should pre-book. Elsewhere, parking costs roughly £13 to £19 for a full day at the nearby car parks, so a station-side stay without a car can save more than the room rate.

Check before you commit

Because prices change, treat everything here as a starting point. Compare the rate for your dates directly with the property, and ask what is included.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

pride-weekend-hotels.title: Blackpool Pride Weekend Hotels | Blackpool.gay
pride-weekend-hotels.description: Where to stay for Blackpool Pride: hotels, guest houses and bars with rooms near the parade and Lord Street party, the 2026 dates and when to book.
pride-weekend-hotels.h1: Where to stay for Blackpool Pride weekend
pride-weekend-hotels.intro: Pride is the busiest weekend of the LGBTQ+ year in Blackpool; pick a stay near the parade and street party, and book early.
pride-weekend-hotels.body_html:
Blackpool Pride fills the town, and the guest houses go first. If you want a hotel near the action, decide on your base early. Below are the stays closest to the Lord Street street party and the walk to the Promenade parade.

When is Blackpool Pride?

The 20th anniversary Pride ran from 5 to 7 June 2026, with the parade on Saturday 6 June at 11am along the Promenade between Burlington Road West and Springfield Road. It also included a free two-day Rainbow Quarter street party along Lord Street, run by more than 20 local businesses. Dates for Pride 2027 have not been announced; check our Pride page and the official Blackpool Pride site for updates. Our seasonal notes describe Pride as usually early June.

Which stays are best for Pride?

  • Pride Lodge: one minute from the station and 2 minutes from Mardi Gras; its own tips say to book early for Pride and Illuminations weekends.
  • Mardi Gras and Q Accommodation: on Lord Street itself, where the street party happens.
  • Trades Hotel and Bar and Welhorny's: men-only, 1 minute from Mardi Gras.
  • Rendezvous Bar and Rooms: near the station, 2 minutes from Mardi Gras.
  • Peek-a-Booze plus Lu-Lu's Cabaret Lounge: lively budget rooms on Dickson Road, 2 to 3 minutes from Mardi Gras.

How early should I book?

Rooms sell out early for Pride, often with three-night minimums according to our season notes. Book as soon as dates are released, and keep a flexible-cancellation option if the property offers it.

How do I get to the parade from my hotel?

The parade runs along the Promenade, a longer walk than the quarter itself: the North Pier is 6 to 10 minutes from most stays and the Tower 11 to 17. Trams run to Blackpool North from the Promenade; check our travel guide and Blackpool Transport for event-day arrangements.

What about the weekend nightlife?

  • Book Funny Girls early; Friday and Saturday sell out first.
  • Mardi Gras together with The Flying Handbag anchor the late-night end of the weekend.
  • Check what's on for any Pride-linked events.

Can I bring a group?

Some guest houses do not take group bookings; see group planning. The Rainbow Quarter reference site has more on past Prides.

Planning your Pride days

Pride weekend runs on three fronts: the festival at the Tower Festival Headland, the Saturday parade along the Promenade and the Rainbow Quarter street party on Lord Street. Stay near the quarter and you can slip from one to the other. Headliners at the 2026 festival included Heather Small, 911 and the Cheeky Girls, and the festival was ticketed.

Pick your base by priority

  • Closest to the parade start: stays on Lord Street and Dickson Road.
  • Quiet retreat: Westfield House or Lawrence House.
  • Late nights: the bars with rooms.

Remember that Pride 2027 dates are not in our data. Keep an eye on our Pride page, which we update when dates are announced.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

illuminations-breaks.title: Illuminations Gay Friendly Hotels | Blackpool.gay
illuminations-breaks.description: Plan an Illuminations break with a gay friendly hotel in Blackpool: 2026 season dates, stays near the pier and autumn drag nights that suit your evenings.
illuminations-breaks.h1: Gay-friendly stays for the Blackpool Illuminations
illuminations-breaks.intro: The lights run into early November, so autumn is a lovely time for a Blackpool break; here are the stays to pick and the dates.
illuminations-breaks.body_html:
The Blackpool Illuminations turn the seafront into a long, glowing night out, and autumn weekends in a gay guest house are a classic. They are busy, so book early.

When are the Illuminations?

Expect the lights from early autumn into the first days of November. The 2026 switch-on happened on 4 September; the main display ended on 1 November, then a shorter run billed as Christmas by the Sea through 3 January 2027. Dates for later years are not in our data, so check the official Blackpool listings.

Which stays suit an Illuminations break?

  • Pride Lodge: its own tips say to book early for Pride and Illuminations weekends. About 9 minutes to North Pier.
  • Lawrence House: the closest in our list to the pier, about 6 minutes, with a roof terrace and evening meals listed.
  • Lu-Lu's Cabaret Lounge and Peek-a-Booze: 7 to 8 minutes to the pier, with rooms above cabaret bars.
  • Chaps Hotel: 8 minutes to the pier, with themed rooms and a bar.
  • Westfield House and De-Lovely Hotel: Lord Street guest houses, about 10 minutes from the pier.

How do I see the lights from my hotel?

North Pier is 6 to 11 minutes on foot from the listed stays and the Tower 11 to 17. The Promenade tram line carries you along the front. Trams run up Talbot Road to Blackpool North; confirm times with Blackpool Transport.

What is on in the evening?

  • Funny Girls staged a Halloween drag spectacular on show nights through 1 November 2026.
  • McGraths hosts a Halloween drag takeover on 31 October 2026, 8pm to 11pm.
  • Garlands has free drag daily from mid-afternoon.

Do rooms cost less than at Pride?

Our season notes call September and October the point for lights at lower prices, but weekends are still busy. Midweek in October is a calmer way to see the display: see quiet midweek breaks.

For a ready-made itinerary, use the 48-hour plan and swap the afternoon for a ride along the lights.

Building an Illuminations evening

A simple pattern works well: an early meal, a stroll or tram along the Promenade as the lights come on, then a show or a bar. Funny Girls doors open at 7pm on show nights, and Garlands offers free drag from mid-afternoon, so you can fit a pint and a performance either side of the lights.

Wrap up

Autumn weather varies, so pack layers. If you are travelling from further afield, our travel guide explains trains, trams and parking. The shorter Christmas by the Sea stretch continues until 3 January 2027 according to our data.

The Illuminations also overlap Halloween, when themed drag shows appear across the quarter. See what's on for specifics.

Which night should I choose?

Weekends are busiest, but our notes suggest autumn is cheaper than Pride. Pick a Wednesday to Sunday when Funny Girls is on if you want a show, or Monday and Tuesday for a quieter pace.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

quiet-midweek-breaks.title: Quiet Midweek Gay Breaks Blackpool | Blackpool.gay
quiet-midweek-breaks.description: A calm midweek gay break in Blackpool: gentle guest houses, plus what is on from Monday to Wednesday, from quizzes and bingo to free daily drag.
quiet-midweek-breaks.h1: Quiet midweek breaks in gay Blackpool
quiet-midweek-breaks.intro: Monday to Wednesday is gentler and cheaper, with quizzes, bingo, karaoke and daily drag; here is where to stay and what to do.
quiet-midweek-breaks.body_html:
If your idea of a Blackpool break is a slow breakfast, a seafront stroll and an easy evening, midweek is perfect. Our season notes call spring the time for a gentler pace, and winter the cheapest time to stay. The scene does not stop, it just breathes.

Where should I stay for a quiet midweek break?

  • Westfield House: small, adults-only, listed as quiet.
  • Lawrence House: four-star, on a quiet street, and evening meals are a good option on a quiet midweek night.
  • De-Lovely Hotel: a breakfast and cocktail bar, open to non-residents with hours that vary by season.
  • Chaps Hotel: a bar and weekly offer if you stay a week.
  • The Prince Albert Hotel: men-only and discreet, with a lounge bar open through the day and evening.

What is on Monday to Wednesday?

DayWhat
MondayThe Flying Handbag Monday Mayhem from 8pm until 3am, karaoke; bingo plus Blankety Blank Wayne hosts it at Peek-a-Booze (from 7pm); inclusive LGBTQ+ football 7pm to 8pm
TuesdayDJ Keiron's 9pm karaoke at Peek-a-Booze
WednesdayQuizMania with Miss Amber 4pm to 8pm at The Flying Handbag, then karaoke; free bingo from 7pm at Peek-a-Booze; Funny Girls show night

Garlands also lists free drag daily, starting in the afternoon. Funny Girls lists show nights Wednesday to Sunday, so Wednesday is the earliest midweek chance. Rendezvous is closed Monday and Tuesday on listed hours, so skip it then.

Is Blackpool dead on a Tuesday?

No, but it is quieter. Tuesday has fewer listed events, so combine karaoke with a seafront walk and an early dinner. Check venue pages before you set out, because smaller bars may trim hours in the quieter months.

Anything different on a Thursday?

Thursday brings Thirsty Thursday at The Flying Handbag, Wayne's karaoke night at Peek-a-Booze, and the monthly LGBTQ+ swimming hour each month on its final Thursday.

Staying a night longer? Link this with our food guide and the budget stays.

A sample midweek day

  1. Breakfast at your guest house.
  2. Stroll the Promenade or visit to the Tower or North Pier.
  3. Afternoon free drag at Garlands.
  4. Dinner at one of the venues in our food guide.
  5. Quiz, bingo or karaoke, depending on the day.

Things to check

Smaller bars may trim hours in quieter months, and some listings do not publish times. Check the venue pages and open tonight before setting out. If you are travelling alone, the quiz and bingo nights are friendly ways to meet people.

Who is midweek best for?

Couples, solo travellers and anyone who prefers talking to shouting over the music. Lawrence House mentions evening meals as a good fit for a quiet night, and a pair of friends can easily fill a Tuesday with a long dinner, a walk and an early finish.

Why midweek works

Midweek means a table at the roast-and-quiz places, a calmer breakfast room and more time to talk to the hosts. It also means fewer venues running late, so plan your evening around the events above rather than wandering in hope.

Staying two or three nights? Spread the show, the quiz and a sauna visit across different evenings, and keep one night free for a long dinner.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

first-time-gay-weekend-blackpool.title: First Gay Weekend in Blackpool | Blackpool.gay
first-time-gay-weekend-blackpool.description: A Blackpool gay weekend for first-timers: where to stay, a Friday to Sunday plan, show booking tips and walking times around the Rainbow Quarter.
first-time-gay-weekend-blackpool.h1: Your first gay weekend in Blackpool, hour by hour
first-time-gay-weekend-blackpool.intro: A 48-hour plan for a first LGBTQ+ weekend in Blackpool: where to base yourself, what to book, and how to pace the nights.
first-time-gay-weekend-blackpool.body_html:
Blackpool rewards a plan, but not a rigid one. Everything in the Rainbow Quarter is a short walk, so your real decisions are where to sleep, what to book and how late you want to go. This plan keeps it simple.

Where should I stay on a first visit?

Pick a base within five minutes of the station. Pride Lodge (1 minute to the station), Mardi Gras (rooms above a community pub) and Q Accommodation (2 minutes) are the easiest starts. Browse the full stays list or stays near the station.

What does the weekend look like?

Friday

  • Get off the train at Blackpool North and leave your luggage at the guest house.
  • Start with a drink on Lord Street, then head to Garlands on Talbot Road, which lists free entry and afternoon-onwards queens.
  • Finish at The Flying Handbag, Queen Street, where Miss Amber hosts on Fridays.

Saturday

  • Slow breakfast, then the seafront: North Pier is roughly 9 minutes from Pride Lodge and the Tower about 12.
  • Early evening: dinner at Garbo's in the Funny Girls building, listed at £29.85 for three courses on show nights.
  • Show: Funny Girls, with 7pm doors and an 8:30pm start on listed times.
  • Afterwards, sing along at Oscars and then try The Flying Handbag.

Sunday

  • Lunch at De-Lovely, Mardi Gras, or The Flying Handbag (noon until 5pm). Book ahead on busy weekends.
  • A final walk along the Promenade before your train.

Do I need to book Funny Girls?

Yes for Friday and Saturday, which sell out first. Standing tickets begin near £10; seat prices vary by night. Phone the box office about access needs.

Is it safe and easy to get around?

The quarter is compact and welcoming; read our safety page and reserve a licensed cab ahead when it is busy. For late-night routes see getting there and getting home.

How do I make it my own?

  • Swap in a pub lunch or food stop.
  • Come midweek for a gentler version: quiet midweek breaks.
  • Check what is open tonight on the day.

The Rainbow Quarter reference site has deeper venue notes if you want more.

A few first-timer rules

  • Bring ID; most venues are 18+.
  • Carry some cash: Lu-Lu's is cash only.
  • Do not expect every place to open all day; times vary, so use open tonight.
  • Men-only venues are men-only: Trades, the Prince Albert, Welhorny's and Growlr Club.

If it rains

Blackpool is built for bad weather: Funny Girls performs inside a 1939 Art Deco cinema that has been restored, the bars are cosy and Garlands has daily drag. A wet afternoon can be a pub afternoon.

Travelling solo or in a couple

Couples of the same sex tend to feel at ease in the quarter and by the seafront, say our notes. Solo visitors often start with quizzes, karaoke or bingo, which are social by design.

What should I pack and book?

  1. Show tickets: book Funny Girls first, as it shapes your Saturday.
  2. Accommodation: decide between a quiet guest house and a bar with rooms, using adults-only guest houses and hotels with a bar.
  3. Dinner: the Garbo's pre-show dinner needs booking with the show.
  4. Travel: check trains on National Rail and trams with Blackpool Transport.

What if I only have one night?

Do the Saturday plan: arrive in the afternoon, enjoy the free drag at Garlands, eat before the show, and finish with karaoke at Oscars. You will still see the heart of the quarter, and the walking times keep the evening easy.

What if I want a men-only weekend?

See men-only hotels for the options, and the saunas listed in our nightlife pages for daytime plans.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

getting-there-and-getting-home.title: Getting to Gay Blackpool by Train & Tram | Blackpool.gay
getting-there-and-getting-home.description: How to reach Blackpool's gay bars and hotels by train, tram or car, and how to get back to your hotel late. National Rail and Blackpool Transport pointers.
getting-there-and-getting-home.h1: Trains, trams and getting back to your hotel late
getting-there-and-getting-home.intro: Blackpool North station is minutes from the gay bars; here is how to arrive, move around and get home safely after a late night.
getting-there-and-getting-home.body_html:
You can reach the Rainbow Quarter without a car. Blackpool North station sits at the quarter's border, and bars and stays are close by. We do not publish timetables here because they change, so use the right sources for times.

How do I get to Blackpool by train?

The principal station is Blackpool North. Our travel notes list direct trains from Manchester, Manchester Airport, York and Leeds, with a change at Preston from London. Check times and engineering works on National Rail before you travel.

From the stationWalk
Pride Lodge1 minute
Q Accommodation2 minutes
Mardi Gras3 minutes
Funny Girlsabout 2 minutes (see venue)
North Pierabout 9 minutes from Pride Lodge
Blackpool Towerabout 12 minutes from Pride Lodge

What about trams?

A tram stop at Blackpool North, beside the station on Talbot Road, links the Promenade line with the quarter. Modern trams are step-free; heritage ones are not. For service patterns and last departures, check Blackpool Transport; do not rely on our notes for late services.

Can I drive and park?

The M55 takes you nearly to the seafront. The open-air car parks on Banks Street and Dickson Road are roughly three minutes away, and Talbot Road multi-storey is around four minutes away. Expect roughly £13 to £19 for a full day, and a multi-day ticket brings the daily rate down. A few guest houses sell cut-price passes, which you must buy before you park. Pride Lodge sells a pass at reception, Westfield House offers vouchers and Lawrence House has no on-site parking.

How do I get home late?

If you are staying in the quarter, you can usually walk: nearly every stay is within 8 minutes of the main bars. Otherwise there are cabs at the station and outside Funny Girls, and a licensed taxi booked in advance is wise at busy weekends. Travel in a group where you can, and keep your hotel's address and phone number handy; read our safety page as well.

Which stays make late nights easiest?

  • Mardi Gras, Trades Hotel and Bar and Peek-a-Booze: rooms in or above the bar.
  • Rendezvous Bar and Rooms: 1 minute to Queen Street.
  • See hotels with a bar.

What if I have access needs?

Heritage trams have steps; stays often have stairs. Phone ahead, and check individual stay pages.

A late-night checklist

  • Save your hotel's address and number on your phone.
  • Agree a meeting point with friends before the last bar.
  • Note taxi ranks at the station and outside Funny Girls.
  • Do not rely on trams for the last journey without checking Blackpool Transport first.

Heading home

Allow time after a big night. If you have a morning train, check National Rail the evening before and pick a stay close to the station; our station list shows the walking times.

Any tips for arriving with a suitcase?

Choose a stay within a few minutes of the platform, check what time the reception is staffed, and tell your host your train. Pride Lodge lists WhatsApp contact out of hours, which helps with late arrivals.

Where do I find up-to-date times?

We deliberately leave out timetables. National Rail has train times and disruption alerts. Blackpool Transport has tram and bus information. Venues themselves publish late opening, and some close earlier than you expect, so check before you rely on a late finish.

Is it better to stay in the quarter?

For late nights, yes. A stay within five minutes of the bars removes most of the transport worry. Our Queen Street stays and station stays pages list the shortest walks.

Arriving by taxi or coach

If you arrive by taxi, give the driver the full address and postcode. Lord Street is FY1 2BD for Q Accommodation and FY1 2BJ for Trades, and Funny Girls is FY1 2AX on Dickson Road.

drag-night-out.title: Drag Shows Blackpool: Plan Your Night | Blackpool.gay
drag-night-out.description: Plan a drag night out in Blackpool: Funny Girls tickets and dinner, free drag at Garlands, Peek-a-Booze nights and booking tips for groups and birthdays.
drag-night-out.h1: How to plan a drag night out in Blackpool
drag-night-out.intro: Blackpool has big-theatre drag, free pub drag and cabaret bars; here is how to pick, book and combine them in one night.
drag-night-out.body_html:
Drag shows in Blackpool come in three flavours: a full theatre production, free drag in a camp pub, and cabaret bars where the host is your friend by the end of the night. You can do all three in an evening.

What are my drag options?

  • Funny Girls (5 Dickson Road): drag cabaret show nights Wednesday to Sunday, with doors at 7pm and the show about 8:30pm to 11:30pm on listed times. Standing from about £10; seats about £17 to £35.
  • Garlands (Talbot Road): free entry and resident queens daily from mid-afternoon.
  • The Flying Handbag: drag hosts including Miss Amber across Thursday and Friday nights, plus Monday Mayhem and QuizMania.
  • Peek-a-Booze, McGraths Bar and Hotel and Lu-Lu's Cabaret Lounge: cabaret bars that also have rooms.

Do you need to book Funny Girls?

Yes for Fridays and Saturdays, which sell out first. Box office hours are listed as Monday to Friday, 9:30am to 5:30pm. Some shows use pyrotechnics and loud bangs, and the venue asks you to phone about access.

Can I have dinner first?

Garbo's pre-show dinner, served in the Art Deco restaurant, is available on show nights, listed at £29.85 for three courses. See our food guide.

What is a good drag evening in order?

  1. Afternoon or early evening: free drag at Garlands.
  2. Dinner at Garbo's, or another venue with food.
  3. Doors at Funny Girls at 7pm.
  4. Aftershow karaoke at Oscars, in the same building, from around 11pm Wednesday to Saturday.
  5. Finish at The Flying Handbag.

What about special seasons?

Funny Girls runs seasonal shows: the Halloween show until 1 November 2026, a New Year's Eve party, and 2027 shows including Spring Fling and Heatwave. Viva Blackpool lists drag brunches on 17 April, 11 September and 18 December 2027, from £39.95. McGraths has a Halloween takeover on 31 October 2026.

Tips for groups

  • Decorating your table or bringing a cake is welcomed at Funny Girls.
  • All venues are LGBTQ+ spaces first, and most are 18+, so bring ID.
  • See group planning and what's on.

Full performer profiles live on the Rainbow Quarter reference site.

Choosing your seats

Funny Girls offers standing and seated tickets, and prices depend on the night. Seats are roughly £17 to £35, so the night you choose changes the cost. For celebrations, ask about table decoration and group arrangements when you book.

Free and cheap nights

If budget matters, Garlands is free, Peek-a-Booze runs free bingo on Wednesdays and Rendezvous lists entertainment from Thursday to Sunday. See our budget stays too.

Stay close

Funny Girls is 1 to 2 minutes from several stays including Rendezvous, Pride Lodge and Q Accommodation, and 2 to 3 minutes from Peek-a-Booze and Trades.

What should I know about venue rules?

Funny Girls is 18+ and some shows use pyrotechnics and loud bangs. Garlands is free to enter. Lu-Lu's is cash only. Check each venue before travelling.

Can I do a drag night on a budget?

Yes. Start at Garlands for free, take standing tickets at Funny Girls from about £10, and finish with karaoke. Peek-a-Booze lists free bingo on Wednesdays.

Can I see drag on a Monday or Tuesday?

Garlands lists daily drag, so yes. Funny Girls runs show nights Wednesday to Sunday on listed times.

How do I pick the right show night?

Think about the mood. Funny Girls is busiest at the end of the week, so expect a full house. Wednesday or Thursday gives you an easier evening and often a simpler booking. Seasonal shows are worth planning around: Halloween, Christmas, New Year's Eve, and the 2027 spring and summer productions all have listed runs.

What happens after the show?

Oscars, in the same building as Funny Girls, has karaoke and live music once the show ends, Wednesday to Saturday. A short stroll takes you to Queen Street and The Flying Handbag, or back to a stay on Dickson Road such as Peek-a-Booze or Lu-Lu's.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

hen-and-birthday-groups.title: Gay Hen & Birthday Groups Blackpool | Blackpool.gay
hen-and-birthday-groups.description: Hen, stag and birthday groups in gay Blackpool: which stays and shows welcome groups, which do not, and how to book respectfully for a big party.
hen-and-birthday-groups.h1: Hen, stag and birthday groups in gay Blackpool
hen-and-birthday-groups.intro: Blackpool is a great celebration town, but the quarter has house rules; here is which stays and shows suit groups and which do not.
hen-and-birthday-groups.body_html:
Birthday parties and hen dos are a Blackpool tradition, and the gay bars are happy to see a good-natured group. They are also LGBTQ+ spaces first, so the best groups arrive respectful and booked ahead.

Which shows welcome groups?

  • Funny Girls: you may dress your table or bring along a cake. Book well ahead for Fridays and Saturdays, and ask about dinner and show bundles.
  • The Flying Handbag: accepts booth reservations for parties, and can lay on a cold buffet when booked roughly a fortnight in advance.
  • Viva Blackpool: lists drag and bottomless brunches through the year; see what's on.

Which stays suit a group?

Bars with rooms are the natural fit if you would like to sleep above the fun: Mardi Gras, Peek-a-Booze, plus Lu-Lu's Cabaret Lounge (about 26 en-suite rooms). Walking times from Lu-Lu's: 4 minutes to Funny Girls, 5 to The Flying Handbag.

Which stays say no to stag and hen groups?

Westfield House is listed as turning away stag and hen parties. Always ask before booking a block of rooms, particularly at the quieter guest houses such as Lawrence House. Our notes say the same about a second guest house, The Gynway.

What are the house rules?

  • Men-only places stay men-only, including Trades Hotel and Bar, The Prince Albert Hotel, Welhorny's and the Growlr Club upstairs at Man Bar. Do not book a mixed group there.
  • Many stays are adults-only, and most venues are 18 or over, so carry ID.
  • Be kind to regulars and performers.

How do I plan a group night?

  1. Pick your show night first; see drag night out.
  2. Book the stay, then the dinner; see food guide.
  3. Agree a late-night meeting point and a way home; see getting home.

Can we choose a quieter date?

Yes: midweek is easier for large tables and cheaper rooms; see quiet midweek breaks.

Practical group tips

  • Book the show first, then match your rooms to it.
  • Give each guest the house rules before arrival.
  • Agree who is the contact for the venue.
  • Ask about deposits and cancellation terms in writing.

A calm celebration

A birthday does not have to be a bar crawl. A Sunday roast, a show and a late drink fit a relaxed pace. Mardi Gras lists a chesterfield lounge as its quiet corner for a chat.

What about the day before and after?

Groups that stay two nights get the best of the town: one night for the show, one for a quieter evening. Quiet midweek dates suit larger parties, and you can check the midweek page for events. On Sunday, lunch at De-Lovely, Mardi Gras or The Flying Handbag rounds things off.

How many rooms are available?

Lu-Lu's lists about 26 en-suite rooms, Trades about 60 (men only), and Q Accommodation seven suites. Ask what each property can hold for your dates.

Is it okay to dress up?

The listed tip is simply to be respectful of performers and regulars. Check with the venue before bringing props, banners or decorations beyond the table decoration that Funny Girls welcomes.

Which nights suit a group best?

For a large group, Friday and Saturday are the biggest draws but the hardest to book. Sunday offers roasts and a quieter pace, and Funny Girls also plays Sunday nights. Mid-afternoon at Garlands suits a warm-up drink with free entry, and the Flying Handbag listed booths suit a seated birthday.

How do I split the bill and the planning?

Ask one person to be the contact for each booking, and share the venue details early. Remember the venues all have different cash and card arrangements: Lu-Lu's is cash only, so agree a plan for the bar tab.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

eat-before-a-night-out.title: Where to Eat Before a Gay Night Out | Blackpool.gay
eat-before-a-night-out.description: Where to eat before a night out in gay Blackpool: pre-show dinner at Funny Girls, Sunday roasts, bar food and bistros, a few minutes from the bars.
eat-before-a-night-out.h1: Where to eat before a night out in the Rainbow Quarter
eat-before-a-night-out.intro: From a three-course dinner before the show to Sunday roasts and daytime bar food, here is where to eat in the quarter.
eat-before-a-night-out.body_html:
A good night out in Blackpool starts with food. These are the venues in our data that serve it, with the times listed so you can build an evening around them.

Where can I have dinner before a drag show?

Garbo's, the Art Deco dining room inside Funny Girls, offers three courses before the show on show nights, between 6pm and 8pm, at £29.85 a head on the listed price. Doors are at 7pm, so book the table when you book the show.

What other venues serve food?

  • The Flying Handbag: food through the day, a sun terrace, and Sunday lunch between noon and 5pm.
  • Mardi Gras: hot food and Sunday roasts; book ahead on busy weekends.
  • Peek-a-Booze: food every day from 9am until 7pm on listed hours.
  • De-Lovely Hotel: Sunday roasts and a breakfast guests praise; its cocktail bar is open to non-residents.
  • Antinous Lounge & Bistro (42 Banks Street): a lounge and bistro on Banks Street, near North Pier.
  • The Blackpool North: a grill and bar that opens at midday and keeps going into the evening.
  • Lawrence House: evening meals listed, handy on a quiet night.

Where is best for a Sunday roast?

Several Rainbow Quarter venues serve roasts every Sunday, among them The Flying Handbag, Mardi Gras and De-Lovely. Reserve ahead; see what's on.

What is a sensible food-then-show timeline?

  1. Early evening: check in and freshen up.
  2. 6pm: dinner at Garbo's, or another venue.
  3. 7pm: doors at Funny Girls.
  4. 11pm: aftershow at Oscars.

Any tips for dietary needs?

We have no dietary details in our data, so phone ahead for allergies and special diets, and ask about cash-only bars such as Lu-Lu's.

Planning a longer trip? Use the 48-hour plan or compare stays above the bar.

Cheap eats and quick bites

If you want something simple, bar food at Peek-a-Booze is listed from 9am to 7pm, and the Flying Handbag serves all day. For something slower, Antinous Lounge & Bistro on Banks Street is steps away from Lord Street.

Before a late night

Eat before 8pm if you are going to Funny Girls, because the show starts around 8:30pm on listed times. If your plan is Queen Street, you have more flexibility.

Which venues combine food and a show?

Funny Girls (via Garbo's) for drag, Mardi Gras for cabaret and karaoke, The Flying Handbag for karaoke, quizzes and drag hosts, and Peek-a-Booze for bingo and karaoke. You can keep the whole evening in one building if you prefer.

What are the mealtimes to remember?

  • Garbo's: 6pm to 8pm on show nights.
  • The Flying Handbag Sunday lunch: noon until 5pm.
  • Peek-a-Booze food: daily 9am to 7pm.

What if I am staying in a guest house?

Many include breakfast, and Lawrence House lists evening meals. Ask your host for suggestions, and see all stays.

Can I eat late?

Hot food in the quarter is mostly early evening or daytime on the listed hours, so plan dinner before the late bars. The Blackpool North's grill and bar opens at midday and runs late, which helps if your timings slip. Always check hours before you rely on a kitchen.

How do I pair eating with walking times?

From Pride Lodge, Mardi Gras and Funny Girls are both about 2 minutes away, and Antinous on Banks Street is about 3. From Lawrence House it is 3 minutes to Funny Girls and 3 to Mardi Gras, so a pre-show meal never has to feel rushed.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.
